title: Pressure rises linearly with depth
caption: Gauge pressure in a liquid is p = ρgh: a straight line from zero at the surface. With ρ = 1030 kg m⁻³ it gains 10.09 MPa for every kilometre, about 1 atm per 10 m. At the bottom of the Mariana Trench (10.9 km) it reaches 110 MPa, about 1100 atm.
alt: Graph of gauge pressure in megapascals against depth in kilometres: a straight line from the origin rising 10.1 megapascals per kilometre to 110 megapascals at 10.9 kilometres.
description: The horizontal axis is depth in km; the vertical axis is gauge pressure ρgh in MPa.
The slope is ρg = 1030 × 9.8 = 10094 Pa per m = 10.09 MPa per km, the same whatever the container's shape.

checks.name: the gradient is ρg = 10.09 MPa per km
